title: Oman Evacuates Injured Crew From Tanker Struck in Hormuz Attack
excerpt: Twelve of the MT On Peace's 19 crew were injured, including 11 Indians, in the latest of at least seven tanker attacks near the strait in early October; India condemned the strike and thanked Oman.
body:
• Oman carried out a medical evacuation of injured crew from the Panama-flagged MT On Peace, which was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with the injured taken to Khasab for treatment.
  • Twelve of the vessel's 19 crew were injured, including 11 Indians; 17 of the crew are Indian nationals, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs.
  • India condemned the attack, thanked Omani authorities for their support, and reiterated its call for an immediate cessation of attacks on shipping in the region.
  • The strike is part of a wave of at least seven tanker attacks near the strait in early October, including the Kuwait-flagged MT Kazimah III, from which five Indians were rescued on October 3.

Oman has evacuated the injured crew of a Panama-flagged oil tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, in the latest violent episode in a waterway that carries a fifth of the world's oil. The country's armed forces said on Tuesday they had carried out a medical evacuation for the crew of the MT On Peace, moving the wounded to Khasab in northern Oman for hospital treatment.

India's Ministry of External Affairs said 12 of the 19 crew aboard the tanker were injured, including 11 Indian nationals. "With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman," the ministry said in a statement on Tuesday. Seventeen of the vessel's 19 crew are Indian nationals.

What happened aboard the MT On Peace

The tanker was struck by an unknown projectile on Monday while passing through the strait, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency, which first reported the attack without naming the vessel. The strike caused a fire in the engine room. Reuters identified the vessel as the MT On Peace, a 114,600-deadweight-tonne LR2 tanker built in 2021, sailing under the Panamanian flag (IMO 9893204).

Its manager, Anglo-Eastern Tanker Management Hong Kong, and operator ONEX DMCC did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Analytics firm Kpler told Reuters the tanker was last seen discharging fuel oil at Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates on August 26 with its transponder switched off.

A week of attacks on the world's most important oil artery

The MT On Peace strike is not an isolated incident. At least seven attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz have been recorded in the first week of October alone, according to reporting citing UKMTO data, which counted seven attacks since September 28. On October 3, five Indian nationals aboard the Kuwait-flagged tanker MT Kazimah III were rescued after that vessel was struck by a projectile in the strait. The Liberia-flagged Lipsi has also been hit.

"The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest."

— India's Ministry of External Affairs

The attacks have rattled energy markets even as crude flows recover. December Brent futures closed at $100.58 a barrel on Tuesday, up 0.26%, while November West Texas Intermediate ended at $89.44. One market report noted that oil shuttles have restored about 80% of Hormuz flows, but prices remain elevated on fears that a renewed rise in merchant-ship attacks could disrupt supplies for the rest of the year.

India's stake: 17 crew, a pattern of rescues

The continuing incidents remain a "cause of deep concern for India," the MEA said, reiterating New Delhi's call for an immediate cessation of attacks on shipping in the interests of peace and stability in the region. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal has repeatedly tied the incidents to the safety of Indian seafarers, who make up a large share of the crews transiting these waters.

The pattern is now familiar. On October 3 the ministry announced the rescue of five Indian nationals from the Kazimah III, stating on X that it remains "committed to the safety, security and welfare of our seafarers abroad." The On Peace evacuation is the largest Indian-crew incident in the strait since, with 11 Indians among the 12 injured.

What's next

No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and the ministry gave no details of the condition of the wounded. Watch for India's next statement on whether it seeks additional assurances for its seafarers, for Oman's account of the evacuation operation, and for whether the pace of attacks — seven in a week — continues. Each strike hardens the insurance and routing decisions that ultimately show up in global fuel prices, and with winter demand rising, the margin for another disruption is thin.
